name: Multi-step form
summary: One form split into steps, checked step by step, with a progress indicator.
description:
Use a multi-step form when a long form falls into clear parts: a quote request, an onboarding flow, a checkout. Keep each step short; if the parts are not really separate, one page is faster.

It is one <form> of .v-wizard-step fieldsets with a .v-steps indicator. Without JS every step shows and the form submits as one. data-v-wizard shows one step at a time: Continue checks the step first (with data-v-validate, using the same inline errors and summary as a submit), Back never checks, steps not reached yet are disabled so they are not checked early, and focus moves to each new step.

classes.name: v-wizard-step
classes.description: One step, a <fieldset>. Hidden and disabled by the JS until it is reached.

classes.name: v-wizard-title
classes.description: The step's <legend>, styled as a heading. It names the step when focus moves to it.

classes.name: v-wizard-actions
classes.description: The Back, Continue and submit buttons. Back sits at the start, the others at the end.

states.description: On the Back and Continue buttons in the markup, so readers without JS see only the submit button.
Set by the JS on the current .v-step; finished steps get .v-step-complete and a hidden "Completed: " prefix.
On the form: the hidden prefix for finished steps (default "Completed: ").

hooks.name: data-v-wizard
hooks.description: Shows one step at a time, checks a step before moving on, keeps the indicator in step and moves focus.

hooks.name: data-v-wizard-back
hooks.description: Goes to the previous step without checking.

hooks.name: data-v-wizard-next
hooks.description: Checks the current step and goes to the next one.

hooks.name: data-v-validate
hooks.description: Gives each step the kit's inline errors and error summary instead of the browser's message.

events.name: v:step
events.description: Fires when a step is shown, including the first.

keyboard.action: In a field, acts as Continue before the last step and submits on the last.
Moves through the current step's fields and the buttons. Focus starts on the step each time it changes.

a11y: Focus moves to the new step, and its legend is announced, so screen reader users know the page changed.
Finished steps say "Completed" in hidden text, not only with the drawn check.
Errors are found step by step, so nobody is told about fields they have not seen yet.
Without JS nothing is hidden: the whole form is there and submits.
